title: Downtown Boston was buzzing in July. Here’s a look at the numbers.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Domestic foot traffic in downtown Boston increased by 10.5% in July compared to July 2025, per Downtown Boston Alliance.
Weekend foot traffic in downtown Boston reached 104% of 2019 levels, with weekday traffic at 75% of pre-pandemic numbers.
Events like the World Cup and new social districts contributed to a 40% sales increase for Temple Place businesses.

title: 2 seriously injured in stabbing near North Station, police say
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Two individuals suffered life-threatening injuries in a stabbing near North Station in Boston.
The incident occurred shortly after 11 a.m. on Lancaster Street, prompting a police response.
The victims were taken to a local hospital; no additional details have been released by police.

title: Healey temporarily restricts kratom sales statewide
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey restricts kratom sales statewide, classifying it as a Schedule I substance with high abuse potential.
Local boards have enhanced authority to enforce the kratom sales ban, effective after a 14-day notice for up to a year.
Kratom's designation affects all forms, unlike federal restrictions which exclude natural products below 7-OH thresholds.

title: Two New England beach towns to visit before the summer ends
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich, Massachusetts, is highlighted as a premier Cape Cod destination with beaches, oyster specials, and sunset cruises.
Ogunquit, Maine, was voted the best beach town in New England and offers various attractions for visitors.
The Deerfield Fair, New England's oldest family fair, is scheduled in Deerfield, N.H., from October 1-4.

title: Diver dies in incident off Cape Cod
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 72-year-old man died in a diving incident off Cape Cod near Sesuit Harbor on Wednesday.
Dennis, Barnstable, and Sandwich fire departments and the U.S. Coast Guard conducted the search operation.
The diver was found around 5:30 p.m. and transported to Sesuit Harbor, where he was pronounced dead.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues after graphic testimony about children’s autopsies
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial continued with graphic testimony about her children’s autopsies, prompting Clancy to break down in court.
Sgt. Kyle Pavao testified about internet searches linked to Clancy's tablet, including topics on suicide methods and psychiatric care.
Clancy, accused of killing her three children, claims postpartum mental illness and voices instructed her to commit the acts.

title: Rhode Island beach house with water views on both sides — can you guess the price?
author: Emily Turner
bullets: Westerly, Rhode Island beach house offers water views on both sides and a contemporary cottage style.
Built in 1987, the 2,724 sq. ft. house has 3 bedrooms and 3 full baths.
The property has private sewer, public water, 2025 taxes of $11,125, with possible price options between $1.78-$1.98 million.

title: 5 best new restaurant openings and dining updates in Boston (August 13, 2026)
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: First Crush, a natural wine bar, to open in mid-September at 259 Washington St. in Somerville.
Tiffani Faison's office-themed bar, The Temp Agency, is now open at High Street Place in Downtown Boston.
The Somerville Fermentation Festival will showcase fermented foods and offer tastings on August 16 at The Center for Arts.

title: 3 concerning trends from Red Sox’ 5-game losing skid
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox suffer a five-game losing streak with tying runs often left on base, struggling against Athletics and Blue Jays.
Boston's offensive performance declines, averaging 2.8 runs per game recently, down from 5.6, with key players underperforming.
Defensive and bullpen issues exacerbate struggles; key reliever Garrett Whitlock has elbow inflammation, potentially requiring an IL stint.

title: An Easton church has been converted to a $1.3m home
author: Megan Johnson
bullets: A historic Easton church at 16 Williams St. has been converted into a $1.3 million residence.
The 5,730 sq ft home includes four bedrooms, three-and-a-half bathrooms, and maintains original church design elements.
The property features a Viking-equipped kitchen, great room with stained glass windows, and a spa-inspired primary suite.
